name: Grand Forks Welding-Machine Co
old_description: Whether you’re looking for a specific part or have an obsolete part, at Grand Forks Welding & Machine we offer custom fabrication, so you don’t have to mess around with going to a manufacturer. We work with you on your specific needs and can fulfill most projects within 2 weeks or less.
about:
Grand Forks Welding & Machine traces its roots to 1885, when a blacksmith shop called Grand Forks Foundry opened in Dakota Territory to repair riverboats. The business evolved over more than a century into the present-day operation in Grand Forks, North Dakota. No founders are named in the available records, and ownership structure is not disclosed.

The company provides custom fabrication, repair, machining, and drive-line services, supplemented by CNC plasma cutting and custom U-bolt manufacturing. It maintains an in-stock inventory of steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and plastics, and runs a fully stocked parts department supplying brands such as Neapco, Weasler, Waterscheid, and Dexter for driveline, PTO, and trailer components. Facility size, headcount, and annual volumes are not published.

The shop serves builders, manufacturers, and agricultural producers — sectors that have relied on its capabilities since the riverboat era. Concrete examples include fabricating new items, repairing existing designs, and supplying replacement parts to keep equipment running in construction, industrial, and farm settings.

The company emphasizes a reputation for high-quality work and responsive service, noting that its highly trained staff can design, build, or repair almost anything a customer requires. The original mission — keeping river traffic moving — expanded into a broader commitment to minimizing downtime for modern industrial and agricultural clients.
